title: Lady Triệu (Triệu Thị Trinh)
summary: Known in Vietnam as Triệu Thị Trinh or Bà Triệu, a woman said to have led an uprising in 248 against the rule of the Chinese state of Wu in Cửu Chân commandery. Her base was Mount Nưa in what is now Thanh Hóa province. Encyclopedia.com has her dying by suicide on Tùng Mountain at about 23; the biographical detail comes largely from tradition and legend.

uncertainty.note: Encyclopedia.com gives birth around 225 and death in 248; the Quân đội nhân dân article, citing legend and divine-record tradition, gives birth in 226. Both sources give 248 for the uprising.

as_recorded.value: Born around 225 ce; lived in the Nui Nua, Thanh Hoa province, Vietnam; committed suicide on Tung Mountain at age 23 in 248 ce

where.modern_name: Núi Nưa (Nưa Mountain), Thanh Hóa Province, Vietnam (pinned to the mountain the sources name as her base; she is said to have died on Tùng Mountain)
where.historical_name: Núi Nưa in Cửu Chân commandery, northern Vietnam, under the rule of the Wu state (Ngô) in 248

importance.justification: Both sources present her as the leader of a 248 rising against Wu rule and as a Vietnamese national figure.

sources.title: Nữ tướng họ Triệu
sources.publisher: Quân đội nhân dân (Sự kiện và Nhân chứng)

reviewer_note: Traditional figure: both sources rely on tradition for her life; birth is c. 225 (Encyclopedia.com) or 226 (legend, per the newspaper). Not checked against the Chinese Sanguozhi or the Đại Việt sử ký toàn thư. The pin is a mountain peak; the newspaper places the rising around both the Nưa and Tùng mountains.
